title: Access contracts runner and enforcement hook for API, runtime and Console
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement an 'access contracts' runtime component that compiles incoming request intent into a normalized contract, evaluates it against RBAC v2 rule graph, and emits an enforcement decision with structured explainability metadata. The component should run as lightweight middleware for the API server, a sidecar for runtime workers, and as a Console enforcement hook. This ticket covers the initial runner implementation, local simulation mode for policy authors, audit enrichment and a minimal admin UI surface in Console to inspect recent decisions.
technical_design: Design goals: (1) Normalize intent across surface areas (API tokens, SSO sessions, service-to-service calls) into a compact AccessContract proto-like JSON; (2) Plug in a pluggable policy evaluation backend (fast in-memory index + optional networked PDP) via a small facade; (3) Emit a single EnforcementPayload containing decision (allow/deny/conditional), reason codes, decision_id, TTL for caching, and an explainable path for Console; (4) Support a simulation mode where enforcement is no-op but decisions are logged for policy authors; (5) Integrate audit enrichment with existing audit pipeline: add fields action_contract, decision_id, eval_latency_ms, and saml_session_anchor when present. Implementation sketch: a thin library 'access-contracts-runner' with adapters for HTTP middleware, GRPC interceptor, and Console plugin. Use existing policy indexer (migration adapter) but implement a temporary translation layer to convert legacy rulesets into contract predicates for parity tests.
tasks: Define AccessContract JSON schema and examples
Implement runner library core: contract builder, evaluator facade, enforcement payload
HTTP middleware adapter for API gateway with prefix-based caching hooks
gRPC / runtime interceptor for worker processes (sidecar-friendly)
Console enforcement hook: display last 25 decisions per org and inspect explainability path
Simulation mode and local CLI policy tester
Audit enrichment: wire enforcement payload into audit sink with extra fields
Create migration adapter to translate RBAC v1 assertions into temporary contract predicates
Unit tests + perf benchmark harness (90th percentile p99 eval < 3ms for common rule shapes)
Integration tests with SAML session binding and admin override flows
Write Ops runbook for rollout and rollback
acceptance_criteria: AccessContract schema published and approved by Security/PM
Runner library exposes middleware/adapters and passes unit tests
API middleware enforces decisions for a small canary org with simulation toggles
Audit events include action_contract, decision_id, eval_latency_ms and saml_session_anchor where applicable
Console shows enforcement events with human-readable reason and link to policy version
Simulation mode produces identical decision traces to enforced mode for identical inputs in canary tests
Perf target: 99th percentile decision eval latency <= 5ms for common rule set on a c5-equivalent CPU (or documented fallback)
risks: Incorrect contract normalization could introduce gaps between API and Console behavior
Evaluation latency spikes for very large rule graphs if fallback PDP is used without caching
Audit volume increases in simulation mode and could impact ingestion pipelines
SAML session attributes vary between identity providers; fragile parsers may miss important anchors
notes: We intentionally keep the runner minimal: policy compilation and heavy indexing remain in Policy Service to allow independent scaling.
Simulation mode will be the primary way to onboard existing customers; we should provide a one-click simulation toggle for Dedicated tenants.
Agree with PM to ship Console visibility scoped to admin roles only (feature flagged) to reduce noise.
